Three refunds, three different routes
Three clients are owed money back this month. They look like one job and they are three, and the screen you happen to be on will suggest the wrong one.

money
You are about to send money back out

The client's balance, the invoice or package behind it, and the month's reported figures. A refund recorded on the wrong route still moves the right amount of money — which is exactly why nobody notices until the month does not reconcile.

The money can be taken back only by asking the client for it. The record can be corrected, but the correction is another document, and the two together are what an auditor reads. Getting the route right the first time costs a minute; getting it wrong costs a reconciliation.

Which of the three situations you are actually in: unused credit the client paid for, an unfinished course of visits, or one payment that should never have been taken. Those are three different documents, not three names for the same one.
Vũ Thị Mai's is not a refund at all

Two of the three are refunds: Lê Thị Bích has credit she paid for and did not use, and Đỗ Văn Hưng stopped a course after 4 of 8 visits. Vũ Thị Mai's 450,000 ₫ is different — she paid once, and a second payment was keyed onto her record by mistake. Nothing is being returned to her; a payment that never should have existed is being reversed. It is the smallest of the three and the only one that is a correction, and it is the one most likely to be recorded as a refund — because it arrives in the same list, on the same screen, with the same client and the same amount of money going the same direction.
